Do you know the history of fractals?

It all goes back to an attempt to measure the coastline of England. The further they refined things, the longer the coastline got. In this, they found all sorts of repeating patterns.

Later, we find this being done again - with a slight twist, in networking computers together. This leads us to Bell Labs and a fella named Mandelbrot. Skipping a little more, we then find that graphics were computationally expensive with computers. Someone realized that fractals were a great way to replicate nature on the fly - namely by making backgrounds for Boeing commercials and presentations. They liked to see the plane mockup fly with a simulated background and mountains were difficult, so they found fractals to be of value and they weren't computationally expensive.

It's from there that you end up with the early stages of 3D gaming and scenery being created on the fly.

All this started with them trying to accurately measure the coastline of England.

I skipped a bunch but Mandelbrot was the first to use the term fractal, but they weren't first originated by him. They go back to at least Georg Cantor (of infinity fame - also famous for having gone insane from thinking about infinity too much) and the "Cantor Set" is also known as a fractal.
